blocks.raw: <Tip>International Style = codified 1932 by Hitchcock and Johnson. Key markers: glass curtain walls, structural frame, rejection of ornament, open plan, flat roofs, pilotis. Dominated 1930–1970s worldwide. Remember: it's NOT all modernism—it specifically rejects all decoration, not just historical ornament.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <Note>The glass curtain wall is both an aesthetic and structural innovation. It's not just a pretty facade—it expresses the structural frame within and eliminates load-bearing walls. The transparency announces modern technology and efficiency. This is the visual signature of the International Style and distinguishes it from earlier modernisms.</Note>

blocks.raw: <Warn>Critical: Don't treat the 1932 MoMA exhibition as the style's endpoint—it's crystallization. The style's influence peaked through the 1960s–70s. Also: don't confuse International Style with all modernism. Art Deco, Streamline Moderne, and International Style are distinct movements. International Style specifically rejects ALL applied decoration, not just ornate historicism. Mies, Le Corbusier, Gropius, and SOM all contributed—it's a collective movement, not a single architect's invention.</Warn>
